heard: When does the new shuttle to the train station begin running?

responses.A: It stops right outside the main entrance.
responses.B: Yes, I take the shuttle every morning.
responses.C: Starting the first of next month.

heard: How much did the catering for last week's client luncheon come to?

responses.A: Accounting hasn't sent us the bill yet.
responses.C: The luncheon was a big success.

heard: Why did Ms. Novak turn down the Lisbon position when she'd been asking for a transfer for years?

responses.A: Because she was never offered the job.
responses.B: Her whole family lives in this city.
responses.C: The transfer forms are on the intranet.

heard: What time is the client call tomorrow, now that it's been delayed three hours from nine o'clock?

responses.A: Nine o'clock, the same as before.

heard: Where did the courier leave the fabric samples that arrived this morning?

responses.A: Ask at the front desk. Lena signed for them.
responses.C: The courier comes at around ten o'clock every day.

heard: How are we getting the display boards to the expo center, now that the company van is in the repair shop?

responses.A: By the company van, as usual.
responses.B: I've booked a rental truck for Thursday morning.

heard: Is the café on the ground floor open on weekends?

responses.A: The ground floor has been repainted.
responses.C: I'll have a coffee with milk, please.

heard: You've booked the interpreter for the Tokyo call, haven't you?

responses.A: Yes, I've been to Tokyo twice.
responses.B: The call went very well last week.
responses.C: Sorry, I thought Hana was handling that.

heard: Didn't the maintenance crew promise to finish the lobby floor before the clients arrive at noon?

responses.A: They told me it'll take until after lunch.
responses.B: Yes, the clients were very impressed last time.
responses.C: No, the lobby is on the first floor.

heard: Is the small conference room still free on Thursday, now that finance has reserved it for the whole afternoon?

responses.A: Yes, I reserved it from two to four o'clock.
responses.C: Finance is hiring two more analysts.

heard: Wouldn't it be cheaper to ship the display units by sea, now that the trade show isn't until next quarter?

responses.A: Yes, because the show starts tomorrow.
responses.B: The display units were designed in Milan.
responses.C: Our warehouse partner only handles air freight.

heard: You're still taking tomorrow afternoon off, aren't you, even with the inspection at three o'clock?

responses.A: Ms. Kemp offered to cover for me.
responses.B: Yes, the inspection was very thorough.
responses.C: No, I don't think it will rain tomorrow.

heard: The invoice from the print shop is higher than the quote.

responses.A: Let me pull up the original estimate.
responses.B: Their print shop is next to the bank.
responses.C: Good, that's less than I expected.

heard: The customer survey scores dropped for the first time in three years.

responses.A: Wonderful, the team will be thrilled.
responses.B: Was it the long waiting times again?
responses.C: The survey only takes about five minutes.

heard: Could you lend me your laptop charger for an hour?

responses.A: The laptops are on sale this week.
responses.C: Sure, it's in the top drawer.

heard: Should we hold the demo in the main hall or the studio, which seats only sixty, now that over two hundred people have registered?

responses.A: I'll see if the main hall is free that morning.
responses.B: The studio is a better fit for a demo.

heard: Why don't we split the dinner bill between the two departments?

responses.A: Because the dinner started at eight o'clock.
responses.B: Marketing has already used up its budget for this quarter.
responses.C: The waiter brought the bill on a tray.

heard: Do you want to go over the budget in the conference room or over lunch?

responses.A: The budget was approved in March.
responses.B: The lunch menu changes every Monday.
responses.C: Let's just do it by phone this afternoon.
